segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time. I pulled up the order form from the CRM. We have you at 42 seats to start, annual term, target go-live on March 18. Does that still match what your team is planning?

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Yep, 42 is right for phase one. We may add another 8 or 10 in Q3, but I don't want those on the initial invoice.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Totally. We'll keep the first invoice to 42 seats only. The pricing sheet has that at $68 per seat per month, billed annually, so $34,272 before tax.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. And implementation is the $4,500 line item, right? I need that broken out separately for finance.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Correct, one-time implementation at $4,500. I can make sure the billing tool shows software and services as separate lines on the invoice.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Great. On terms, legal was fine with 12 months, but they asked for net 45 instead of net 30. Is that something you can do?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, net 45 is within our standard range for annual contracts. I don't need deal desk for that. I'll update the order form before I send it over.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Perfect. If we sign by Friday, can we still make the March 18 go-live?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes. If signature is in by February 23, onboarding can kick off the week of February 26. That gives us three weeks for setup, admin training, and the data import.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Sounds good. Send the revised order form and I'll route it for signature today.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. I'll send it in the next half hour with the 42 seats, annual billing, net 45, and the implementation line separated.
